validation.notes: Repaired three cooperating faults that broke the pre-consent boundary: (1) SettingsManager.loadFromStorage ignored its projectTrusted argument (gate replaced by `if (false)`), so untrusted managers still parsed and merged cwd/.pi/settings.json; restored `if (scope === "project" && !projectTrusted) return {}`. (2) DefaultResourceLoader.loadProjectTrustExtensions forced `setProjectTrusted(true)` during the bootstrap pass, contradicting its own comment; now forces `false`, so the trust callback and package-manager resolution see only global/user and temporary CLI resources. (3) resolveProjectTrusted used a truthiness test on `trustOverride`, so an explicit `--no-approve` (false) fell through to the extension hook, saved trust store, defaultProjectTrust and the interactive prompt; now `if (options.trustOverride !== undefined)`. The regression script links the three real production modules in one createGraph VM graph (resource-loader.ts + settings-manager.ts + project-trust.ts) and fakes only the boundaries: DefaultPackageManager (mirrors the real gating rule, project resources only while settingsManager.isProjectTrusted()), loadExtensionsCached/createExtensionRuntime/loadExtensionFromFactory, loadSkills/loadPromptTemplates/loadThemeFromPath/findGitPaths/createEventBus/resetTimings/createSourceInfo, emitProjectTrustEvent/getProjectTrustOptions/hasTrustRequiringProjectResources, chalk/config/utils paths, an in-memory SettingsStorage, a trust store and a prompt UI. Six scenarios assert 6/6: untrusted SettingsManager exposes global-only settings with {} project settings while a trusted transition/reload admits project settings with nested compaction inheritance intact; explicit trustOverride false wins over a saved approval plus defaultProjectTrust 'always' without calling ui.select or writing the trust store; explicit true wins over a saved denial; saved decisions and headless sessions keep their behavior; bootstrap returns only [cli, global] extensions and leaves the project untrusted; a trusted reload decides trust from [cli, global] only then admits the project extension and project settings; an explicit false override routed through the real resolveProjectTrusted keeps project resources out and prompts nobody; a saved approval still admits project resources without prompting. Mutation check: restoring any single one of the three files to its faulty baseline makes the script fail with a genuine AssertionError (settings-manager -> 'project settings must not be read before consent', resource-loader -> 'the pre-consent bootstrap must load only global and temporary CLI extensions', project-trust -> 'an explicit false override must win over saved trust'); no crash, import error or timeout was involved. Asynchronous ordering is controlled with awaited promises only - no timers, randomness, network or external services. Test fixtures are created under .prale-eval/fixture/ and removed in a finally block. Limitation recorded: the repository's own suites (vitest, tsgo, scripts/check-*.mjs) and biome cannot run here because no dependencies are installed (node_modules absent: ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND for 'typescript'); no dependency was installed, and the edited TypeScript sources load successfully through Node 24 stripTypeScriptTypes via .prale-eval/subject.mjs.
